correctness.rationale: The path between leaves has length two so the graph seminorm is the maximum hub–leaf difference. At f(0)=0 its unit ball is the independent leaf cube; an edge row difference is maximized in absolute value by choosing matching signs on the leaves. Subtracting the two normalized rows over Z_0 Z_i gives the positive distinguished-leaf difference (1-q^2)b_i(a+qS_i), and the opposite-signed differences (1-q^2)qb_i b_j at other leaves (these are numerators, with common denominator Z_0 Z_i). The sum of magnitudes is the stated expression and the indicated sign potential attains it. Subtracting one puts q times [b_i(S_i-b_i)-a^2-2aBq-S_i(S_i+3b_i)q^2] over the positive same denominator. This bracket strictly decreases on q>=0 even for S_i=0. A nonpositive initial value gives strict contraction on every 0<q<1, including equality in the mass criterion. A positive initial value gives a unique root below one since C_i(1)=0. The maximum of the individual roots therefore gives exactly the claimed strict, boundary and expansive regimes. Equal masses give initial sign m-3, with first threshold (-4+sqrt(34))/18. Direct substitution a=1/10,b=(1,9),q=1/100 makes the first edge bracket positive, verifying expansion already with three vertices. W1 is below 2 because the diameter is at most 2 and positive rows have common mass; the stated m-to-infinity sequence q=m^(-3/4) sends mq to infinity and mq^2 to zero, so the coefficient approaches 2. The matrix q^d is the strictly positive definite covariance of an invertible linear transform of independent unit-variance variables; multiplying by the positive diagonal factors sqrt(w_i/Z_i) gives the symmetric matrix similar to K_q. Thus π proportional to wZ is reversible and all eigenvalues are positive, including in the expansive examples. These exact calculations settle the claim.
